title: Pelvic ultrasound
what: The doctor looks at your uterus and ovaries with ultrasound. The probe is placed on your belly or put into the vagina. It is safe and uses no radiation.
why: For pain in the lower belly, period problems, planning a pregnancy, or a routine checkup.
tell_doctor: The first day of your last period
If you have never had sex. Then the probe is not put into the vagina
If you have a coil (IUD) or have had surgery

prepare.title: Cycle day
prepare.text: Usually on day 5 to 7 of your cycle, unless the doctor gives another day. Sometimes you need to come in the second half of the cycle.

prepare.title: Through the belly
prepare.text: You need a full bladder. Usually drink 1 liter of water an hour before and do not go to the toilet.

prepare.title: Through the vagina
prepare.text: Here you empty your bladder before the scan instead. Check with your clinic which way you will have.

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: A normal shower. You can bring a pad with you.

bring: A sheet and tissues, if the clinic does not provide them
steps: You undress below the waist and lie on the couch
Through the belly: gel is put on your lower belly and the probe is moved over it
Through the vagina: a disposable cover with gel is put on a thin probe, and it is gently inserted
The doctor looks at the uterus and ovaries from different angles
feel: Through the belly: pressure on your full bladder. It can be uncomfortable
Through the vagina: usually not painful, much like a gynecology exam
If it is unpleasant, tell the doctor
after: You can go back to your day straight away
You may have a little discharge from the gel
You usually get the report right away
red_flags: Severe lower belly pain, heavy bleeding, weakness, or fainting: do not wait for your appointment. Call emergency services

faq.q: On which day of my cycle should I have a pelvic ultrasound?
faq.a: Usually on day 5 to 7. But if the doctor is looking for something specific, they may choose another day.

faq.q: Can I have an ultrasound during my period?
faq.a: Sometimes yes, if the doctor asks for it. For a routine checkup, it is better after your period ends.

faq.q: Is a transvaginal ultrasound done if I have never had sex?
faq.a: No. The scan is done through the belly with a full bladder, or another way the doctor suggests.

reminders.text: Pelvic ultrasound soon. If it is through the belly, drink 1 liter of water an hour before and do not go to the toilet.
